summary: Former Louisiana tower in East Baton Rouge Parish, near Pride; Wikipedia lists it as torn down. No build, staffing or site record found.

facts.status_note: Wikipedia's list says torn down; the tower is missing from a map that still showed it in 2012, and no source describes the site now.

events.note: Appears on a 2012 map, according to the Wikipedia list's note
Removed from the map by 2015, according to the Wikipedia list's note; tear-down date not given

evidence.supports: tower lies in East Baton Rouge parish

evidence.quote: at an elevation of 134 ft MSL

evidence.supports: can be seen on the USGS 1:24K topographic map for Pride, Louisiana
evidence.quote: It can be seen on the USGS 1:24K topographic map Pride, LA

evidence.supports: funds directed to fire protection from 1915 allowed hiring lookout watchmen or patrolmen
evidence.quote: In 1915 funds were directed for fire protection work allowing the hiring of lookout watchmen or patrolmen.

evidence.supports: first steel fire tower built near Bogalusa in 1922
evidence.quote: In 1922 the first steel fire tower was built near Bogalusa on Great Southern Lumber Company land.

evidence.supports: Pride tower listed as torn down
appears on 2012 map, removed from 2015 map, visible on Street View before decommission
evidence.quote: As with others, appears on 2012 map, removed from 2015 map. Visible here on Google Street View prior to decommission.

evidence.supports: TopoQuest describes the tower in the present tense
evidence.quote: Pride Lookout Tower is a tower located in East Baton Rouge County, LA

resolved_conflicts.explanation: TopoQuest writes in the present tense from a map listing. The Wikipedia list records the tower as torn down and missing from the 2015 map. The story follows the Wikipedia list.

sources.title: List of fire lookout towers in Louisiana

notes_for_editor: Brief record checks out: county, coordinates and gone status match Wikipedia. Tear-down date, build date, design, height, agency and staffing are not in any source read. TopoQuest's 134 ft elevation has no matching facts key, so it appears only in the story. The firetower.org Louisiana former-sites register (six entries) does not list Pride. Anyplace America returned HTTP 403 and nhlr.org reset the connection; neither was retried. Google Street View was not checked. Used three web searches, one over the two-search budget. Possible follow-up: Louisiana Office of Forestry records or local newspaper coverage of the tower's removal.
